## Step 3: helpers reimplemented elsewhere (graphty-element, graphty, graph-format, graph-io, compact-mantine, tools, visual-review)

This is a review for logic that does the same job as a helper already in the repository, which SonarQube's copy detector cannot see. Line numbers are against master as of 2026-10-02.

### Fixed (PR refactor/reuse-existing-helpers)

- graphty-element: the colorblind simulation's hex-to-RGB and RGB-to-hex now come from `utils/styleHelpers/color/interpolation.ts`. The style encoding's `hold()` is now `scales.ts`'s `clamp()`.
- graphty: `utils/color-utils.ts` and `SWATCH_COLORS_HEXA` now come from `@graphty/compact-mantine`.
- graphty: `titleCase`, `pluralise`, `isFiniteNumber` and `formatValueForClipboard` were each written twice and now live once.
- compact-mantine: DataTable's `clampNumber` is now navigation's `clamp`.
- graph-io: the GML exporter's pass-through `gmlRealText` is gone; it calls `formatGmlReal`.
- visual-review: `accept.mjs` uses `compare.mjs`'s `sha256`.

### Left for a decision

Each item below differs in behavior, needs a helper made public first, or belongs in another package.

graphty-element
- `src/simple/defineLayout.ts:113` `seededRandom` is the same mulberry32 as `algorithms/src/utils/math-utilities.ts:8`. That one is not exported from `@graphty/algorithms`.
- `src/session/styles/legend.ts:315` `isColorValue` overlaps `channels.ts:145` `asColorValue`, whose own comment says one guard should exist. The legend version is stricter: it also requires `hex` to be a string.
- `src/session/commands/config.ts:104` and `src/session/runs/runId.ts:113` are each a plain-object check. `graph-format/src/columns/column.ts:136` `isPlainObject` does the same job but is not exported. `config.ts` also rejects null-prototype objects, which the other two accept.
- `src/session/project/strict.ts:99` `checksum` is a hand-rolled FNV-1a over a typed array. `graph-format/src/snapshot/hash.ts:148` `hashTypedArray` does that job but is not exported, and its output shape differs.
- `Math.max(0, Math.min(1, x))` is written inline about 12 times in `src/utils/styleHelpers` (size, edgeWidth, opacity, diverging, interpolation). They could share `clamp`.

graphty (app)
- `src/components/sidebar/panels/StyleLayerPropertiesPanel.tsx:124` `colorOf` builds `#RRGGBB` from an Rgba by hand, without clamping. graphty-element's `toColorValue` (`src/session/styles/channels.ts:169`) does this properly but is not exported from any entry point. The fix is to export it from `@graphty/graphty-element/catalog` and then use it here.
- `src/components/sidebar/controls/` (CompactColorInput, CompactCheckbox, ControlSubGroup, EffectToggle, StyleNumberInput, StyleSelect, about 575 lines) holds older copies of compact-mantine components. Nothing outside their own tests imports them. They should be deleted along with their tests and the entry in `src/components/__tests__/compact-css-regression.test.tsx:40`.
- `src/components/demo/CompactComponentsDemo.tsx:80-102` parses and composes HEXA inline. compact-mantine's `parseHexaColor` and `toHexaColor` differ: they accept shorthand, and the demo upper-cases.
- `src/constants/style-options.ts:15` `StyleOption` duplicates compact-mantine's `StyleSelectOption` type on purpose.
- `src/components/shell/canvas/Minimap.tsx:99-123` is a hand-written `useThrottledValue`. `@mantine/hooks` has one; check its trailing-edge timing before swapping.
- Two count formatters: `shell/statusbar/formatCounts.ts:108` `formatExactCount` clamps negatives, `shell/readings/readingFormat.ts:43` `formatCount` keeps the sign.
- Two percent formatters: `shell/statusbar/loadingPhases.ts:98` clamps to 0..1, `readingFormat.ts:80` does not.
- Two metric formatters: `shell/analysis/nodeMetrics.ts:524` and `shell/readings/nodeMetricReading.ts:201` both implement the same spec rule but print differently. The first drops trailing zeros and adds separators; the second does neither. The same metric can therefore read differently in a bin label and in a reading.

graph-io / graph-format
- `graph-io/src/common/text.ts:19-56` (`inferTextDtype`, plus `kindOfValue` and `textDtypeRank`) reproduces `graph-format/src/columns/infer.ts` on purpose, per its header. Sharing it needs graph-format to export these.
- `graph-io/src/formats/pajek/exporter.ts:523` `idText` and `formats/dot/exporter.ts:869` `idToText` are identical, but neither is shared. They could move to `src/common`.

tools / visual-review
- `visual-review/trusted/lib/serve.mjs:1196` and `visual-review/trusted/gate.mjs:317` inline the same SHA-256 hex. `gate.mjs` must stay dependency-free, so this needs a dependency-free hash module before they can share it.
- `tools/diff-stories.mjs:52-102` (static server and MIME map) is the same job as `visual-review/capture/capture.mjs:252-276`. capture's version is not exported, and visual-review's `exports` map exposes nothing else.
- Listing workspace packages from `pnpm-workspace.yaml` is written three times: in `tools/check-declared-build-tools.mjs`, `tools/check-legacy-use.mjs` and `tools/check-published-deps.mjs` (`workspacePackages`). The third parses more loosely.
- Walking source files is written twice: `tools/check-legacy-use.mjs` and `tools/check-data-source-migration.mjs` both have a `sourceFiles`, with different extension filters.

Not covered here: webgpu-graph-algorithms, algorithms/src and layout/src, which another session is changing right now.

Most of what SonarQube still reports is declarative tables (rows with the same fields and different values in channels.ts, catalog/algorithms.ts, bindings.ts) and deliberately repeated test fixtures; folding them would make them harder to read. Generated sample data is excluded from the count once #725 lands. If any item differs, only those come back undecided. Once passkey approval is enforced (#670), this becomes a single Face ID prompt with no review screen, since the server cannot sign for the owner.

Additions from #737 (closed as a duplicate of this issue), after #490 was blocked on 2026-10-02 by baseline-only merge conflicts with master:

- **Cover the conflicted case, not only the stale one.** A pull request whose branch cannot merge because master and the pull request changed the same baseline PNGs should get the same "Update from master" action, even before any capture: merge master (never rebase), take master's side for every conflicting file under the baselines directory, one signed commit naming the files, push, and say which stories CI will recapture. Any conflict outside the baselines directory: refuse and list the files.
- **A CLI command too:** `visual-review update <pr>` does the same from a terminal.
- **Approval:** the step accepts nothing (it restores master's already-approved images, and the gate makes the owner review whatever still differs), so it should not need a passkey. Confirm against the gate's record replay before building; if a record is needed, design it rather than skip it.
- **Why it matters:** agents are barred from writing under visual-baselines/, so without this the owner has to merge by hand; on #490 the permission classifier refused both the merge and the push.
- **githerd** should detect "conflicts only in baselines" and "capture stale against master" while polling and put the update on the owner's list, linking to this action.

## Addition: stop the stock controls from being used by accident (owner, 2026-10-01)

We cannot deprecate Mantine's own exports, so the guard goes into our own lint:

1. **A lint rule in the graphty app and in compact-mantine** (ESLint `no-restricted-imports`, beside the app's own rules in `graphty/eslint-rules/`) that fails any import of `ColorInput` or `ColorPicker` from `@mantine/core`, with the message "Use CompactColorInput from @graphty/compact-mantine." It runs in lint, the pre-push hook and CI. compact-mantine's own `CompactColorInput` (and `ColorPickerPanel`, if it needs Mantine primitives) is the only allowed exception, written as a narrow per-file override, not a disable comment.
2. **The rule's list is the place to record every replacement**: wherever compact-mantine has its own component for a job a stock Mantine component also does, add that pair to the same rule.
3. **Docs for third parties**: compact-mantine's documentation gets a short "Use these instead of Mantine's" table naming each replacement. Our lint rule does not run in other people's projects, and they may legitimately want Mantine's components. Once the theme stops styling `ColorInput` (above), a stock `ColorInput` renders as plain Mantine.
4. **No runtime warnings** in the stock components; they keep working as Mantine documents them.

Done when, in addition to the list above: the lint rule is in place, a test proves it fails on a `ColorInput` import, and the docs table exists.

I measured this before building it. A GPU Louvain made of the existing parts (group-by-key for the move pass, the device graph build for the contraction) loses to the CPU port on realistic graphs at every size graphty-element holds, so I did not build it.

These were timed on the RTX 4070 SUPER at load averages of 5 to 11. The CPU arm is the real port. The device arm was costed from per-level timings on the card: one group-by pass, one device graph build and one readback, on every level of a simulated synchronous Louvain.

| graph, nodes / edges | Chromium: CPU / device | speedup | Node speedup |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| LFR 10,000 / 101,905 | 19.0 / 42.8 ms | 0.44x | 1.09x |
| LFR 50,000 / 91,496 | 31.3 / 48.9 ms | 0.64x | 1.25x |
| G(n, m) 10,000 / 100,000 | 45.5 / 37.4 ms | 1.22x | 1.05x |
| G(n, m) 20,000 / 100,000 | 36.5 / 45.8 ms | 0.80x | 1.86x |
| G(n, m) 50,000 / 100,000 | 45.2 / 68.8 ms | 0.66x | 1.81x |
| LFR 100,000 / 1.0M | 149 / 88 ms | 1.70x | 1.70x |
| G(n, m) 100,000 / 1M | 362 / 117 ms | 3.11x | 3.22x |
| LFR 1M / 10.1M | -- | -- | 3.42x |
| G(n, m) 1M / 10M | -- | -- | 4.11x |

- **The group-by rate is fine:** 0.13 to 0.75 ns per arc.
- **The contraction loses.** A device graph build costs at least 5.6 ms in Chromium, because of its two round trips, and Louvain contracts 4 to 8 times.
- **Inside the element's 50,000-node / 100,000-edge ceiling** it loses on both graphs with community structure (LFR). Its one win there (1.22x) is on a uniform random graph, where its partition is also worse (modularity 0.147 against 0.180).
- **A contraction with a single round trip per level** would still give only 1.2x to 2.4x inside the ceiling.
- **Above the ceiling it earns,** 1.7x to 4.1x.

The full method and table are in the decision record, in #656.

Three things would reopen this: a raised element ceiling (#419), a faster Chromium round trip, or a contraction that needs no readback of its own.

comments.body:
## Audit: graphty-element 1.10.5 against the commit the visual baselines were seeded from

**What was compared.** I built graphty-element's Storybook at the last 1.x release (`graphty-element@1.10.5`) and at 22a83a8a4, the commit the owner-reviewed visual baselines were seeded from. Changes after that commit already went through the visual review, so master was not part of this comparison. Both builds were captured on the same machine with `tools/diff-stories.mjs` at 1200 x 900, using headless Chromium with SwiftShader, and compared with `tools/pixel-diff.mjs` at its default threshold. Neither tool was modified. The comparison covers all 150 stories that exist in both builds, across 25 story titles. 18 render identically above the threshold and 132 differ.

**What changed, and why.** Each group below is a named change between the two commits:

- **Camera framing (53 stories, mostly the 20-node graph behind the Styles, Algorithms and Label stories).** Node positions are identical. The camera sits about 1% farther back (z -63.87 to -64.55), so the picture is a pixel or two smaller. Cause: zoom-to-fit now frames nodes by their size with no extra margin, and frames labels only on zoom-to-fit (e2cbde72c, 08373f468), plus the camera floor and presets (0b81d8ff4). Intended.
- **Labels (all 28 Label stories and every story with node names).** Text sits slightly closer to its node, and panels are sized a little smaller. Cause: label panels are now sized from font metrics (4d2362b32), and label textures are rasterized on the CPU so every load draws the same pixels (8c3f6b61f). Intended. The label font was not pinned in 1.10.5, so these stories were checked by eye rather than by pixel count. Nothing was missing or clipped.
- **Algorithm colors and sizes (Centrality, Combined, Community, Component, Flow, Spanning Tree, Shortest Path, Traversal).** Results use the new default palettes (d1423a369) and size by a run's metric (821b6e3b2). Connected Components drew every node the same blue in 1.10.5 and now colors each component, which is a fix.
- **Kamada-Kawai, 2D and 3D.** The layout is very different. 1.10.5 stopped near its circular start with long crossing edges, and now it converges. Cause: the solver no longer steps uphill (0f3bd5479), the L-BFGS sign is fixed (19fc929e4), and 3D starts from a seeded random layout with the full pairwise cost (501cc90dd, #99). Intended.
- **Spring and ForceAtlas2 (2D and 3D).** The same shape, with nodes moved by up to 10 world units. Cause: the layouts now receive edge weights (5f444b731), and these stories use the weighted Les Miserables graph. Intended.
- **Arrowheads.** Arrowheads now take their line's color unless told otherwise. The 2.0 arrow and edge commits are b8ac1d4f3, 3615e18dd and 635c399c4. Intended.
- **Story changes rather than rendering changes.** The Selection stories now select "Alpha" in their play function. All Node Shapes now lists every shape in the schema, so torus appears. Large Graph Physics250 switched from ngraph to ForceAtlas2 on a different generated graph. Bipartite Matching draws matched edges wider. These pictures differ because the stories changed.

**The edge-line difference.** Horizontal and vertical edges are pixel-identical between the two builds. Only diagonal edges changed, and they are slightly wider in 2.0: a 10 px, 45-degree edge in `Styles/Layered` Arrow Head Styles has a horizontal run of 16.00 px in 1.10.5 and 16.75 px at the seed, while the vertical edge next to it measures 10.5 px in both. The cause is b8ac1d4f3, which fixed #124. 1.x took the edge's perpendicular in clip space, where x and y have different pixel scales on a non-square canvas, so diagonals came out thinner than their width. 2.0 takes the perpendicular in pixels. The error grows with the canvas's aspect ratio, which is why a capture at a different viewport could show more than the under-one-pixel difference measured here. I could not reproduce a 10 px difference at this viewport. This is a fix, not a regression, so nothing was filed against the instanced-edge pull requests (#490, #617). The one thing they need to keep is the pixel-space perpendicular.

**What was filed.**

- #708: max flow's suggested styles lost edge width by flow. In 1.10.5 the busiest mains were drawn wider, from 2.5 to 4 px. In 2.0 every edge is 2 px and only the color varies, including in master's approved baseline. The story's own comment still says the mains are drawn at "different widths". Cause: 13125c769 removed the hand-written suggested styles, and the shared derivation can suggest a size only for node metrics.

**What the owner needs to look at.**

1. #708: decide whether edge metrics should be able to ask for width, the way node metrics ask for size.
2. One note, not filed: in Large Graph Physics250 the camera is now far enough back that the 150-node graph's edges taper below a pixel and look broken. Lines taper with distance in both versions by design, so this comes from the story's new layout, not from the renderer. Say if you want the story framed closer.

Nothing was accepted in Chromatic or the visual review, and no baseline or story was changed.

The audit is complete (comment above). It found one real regression, filed as #708 (max flow no longer draws edge width by flow); the other differences were reviewed and are expected. Closing the audit; #708 tracks the fix.

comments.body: Seen again in the pre-push gate on a branch that changes only .github/workflows/release.yml: the four ai.test.ts tests (getGraphtyElement loads and caches the module, getApiKeyManager returns the class and creates instances) timed out at 15 s on the dynamic import of ../ai, while about ten other pre-push gates were running on the machine (load average 85 to 110). The rest of the graphty suite passed, 115 of 116 files.

Measurements from the branch of PR #512, which adds a graphty test that mounts the real graphty-element. They point to a slow import rather than a hung one.

The first test's time is almost all the `await import("../ai")`. Durations of `ai.test.ts`, same machine and warm cache:

- alone: 1.8 s
- side by side with only the new real-element test file: 8.4 s
- full graphty suite on master's test set, earlier the same hour: 8.1 s
- full graphty suite, with the real-element file held until the rest had finished, load average 78: 14.6 s, 0.4 s under the 15 s default browser test timeout
- the same full suite with the real-element file running alongside: over 15 s, then the `invalidateModule` cascade described above

Every test file of a vitest browser project runs as an iframe in the same page. Those iframes share one renderer main thread. The import has to transform and evaluate a large module graph on that thread, so how long it takes depends on what every other file is doing and on how loaded the machine is. Past 15 s the test times out while the import is still in flight, and `vi.resetModules()` then throws in every later `beforeEach`.

PR #512 keeps its own heavy file off that thread by running it in a separate project after the others (`sequence.groupOrder`). That does not fix this issue, which still needs one of two things: the first test should stop paying for a whole-bundle import inside a test body, or the cascade after a timeout needs to be understood.

Seen again at 03:15 today in the pre-push gate for a README-only change to algorithms: 'getGraphtyElement > loads the graphty-element module' timed out at 15000 ms on the dynamic import of ../ai, with load average about 67 and a dozen pre-push gates running at once. Only that one test failed in this run.

comments.body:
## Render-ceiling measurement, 2026-09-26

Harness: `tmp/load-10k/load-time.ts` from the gpu-p8 worktree, extended to sample the Chromium process tree (renderer and GPU process RSS every 2 s), read `performance.memory`, probe whether the renderer's main thread still answers, and cap a load that never returns. Headless Chromium on the RTX 4070 SUPER through ANGLE/Vulkan, `layout="random"`, `acceleration="off"`, default style (an arrow head on every edge). Box load average 5-33 during the runs (it is shared); the numbers below are single runs, and the crash rows reproduced on every attempt (three at 18k, two at 20k).

### What freezes

The renderer process **dies**; it does not hang. In every "frozen" row the renderer disappeared from the process tree 20-26 s in, the GPU process dropped back to a few hundred MB, and `page.evaluate(() => 1)` never answered. There is no kernel OOM entry: the box has 61 GB free. The limit is V8's own: `performance.memory.jsHeapSizeLimit` reads **3,586 MB** in this Chromium, and a 16 GB `--max-old-space-size` does not move it (which is why the earlier 16 GB experiment changed nothing).

Master, 10 edges per node:

| nodes / edges | scene meshes | materials | JS heap used after load | renderer RSS peak | GPU process RSS peak | load |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5,000 / 50,000 | 105,002 | 50,003 | 1,373 MB | 1.7 GB | 1.0 GB | 5.9 s |
| 8,000 / 80,000 | 168,002 | 80,003 | 1,965 MB | 2.4 GB | 1.5 GB | 5.6 s |
| 10,000 / 100,000 | 210,002 | 100,003 | 2,356 MB | 2.9 GB | 1.8 GB | 6.8 s |
| 12,000 / 120,000 | 252,002 | 120,003 | 2,995 MB | 3.4 GB | 2.1 GB | 8.2 s |
| 15,000 / 150,000 | 315,002 | 150,003 | **3,586 MB = limit** | 4.2 GB | 2.5 GB | 12.6 s |
| 17,000 / 170,000 | 357,002 | 170,003 | **3,586 MB = limit** | 4.5 GB | 2.9 GB | 19.4 s |
| 18,000 / 180,000 | -- | -- | -- | 4.7 GB, then the process died | 2.8 GB | never |
| 20,000 / 200,000 | -- | -- | -- | 4.4 GB, then the process died | 1.2 GB | never |

The heap is pinned at its cap from 15,000 up, so every load past that point is garbage-collection bound (12.6 s, then 19.4 s for 13 % more edges), and one step further the allocation fails and the renderer is gone.

Which count matters:

| nodes / edges | edges per node | JS heap | renderer RSS | load |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 200,000 / 0 | 0 | 1,965 MB | 2.2 GB | 2.6 s |
| 100,000 / 0 | 0 | 1,144 MB | 1.3 GB | 5.0 s |
| 8,500 / 170,000 | 20 | -- | 4.5 GB | 21.1 s |
| 34,000 / 170,000 | 5 | -- | 4.6 GB | 24.7 s |
| 9,000 / 180,000 | 20 | -- | 4.7 GB (survived, barely) | 22.5 s |
| 50,000 / 100,000 | 2 | 2,661 MB | 3.5 GB | 8.0 s |
| 100,000 / 100,000 | 1 | 2,995 MB | 3.7 GB | 11.4 s |

Roughly 20 KB of heap per edge and 10 KB per node. Nodes are one InstancedMesh each (instances of one source mesh) and are cheap; an edge is a line InstancedMesh, an arrow-head Mesh and a ShaderMaterial of its own, and the material is the expensive part in both processes: the GPU process holds 2.8 GB of per-material state at 170k edges.

### Does PR #394 (instanced arrow heads, one material per batch) remove the cliff?

It moves it. Same harness on `origin/fix/instanced-arrowheads-per-scene-uniforms` merged with master (one comment-only conflict):

| nodes / edges | scene meshes | materials | JS heap | renderer RSS peak | GPU process RSS peak | load |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 15,000 / 150,000 | 315,003 | 4 | -- | 3.1 GB | 0.31 GB | 9.3 s |
| 18,000 / 180,000 | 378,003 | 4 | -- | 3.6 GB | 0.35 GB | 11.9 s |
| 20,000 / 200,000 | 420,003 | 4 | 3,586 MB = limit | 3.8 GB | 0.34 GB | 10.8-13.2 s |
| 25,000 / 250,000 | -- | -- | -- | 4.4 GB, then the process died | 0.24 GB | never |
| 30,000 / 300,000 | -- | -- | -- | 4.35 GB, then the process died | 0.20 GB | never |

So #394 takes the GPU process from 2.8 GB to 0.35 GB and lets 18k and 20k load, but the heap is at its cap again at 200k edges, because each arrow head is still an InstancedMesh object in `scene.meshes` (420,003 of them). The next step the issue names, one mesh per style with thin instances or a merged line system, is what removes the per-edge JS object and is the change that would move this by an order of magnitude.

### What lands now

`DEFAULT_LIMITS` is set to `renderCeiling: 50_000` nodes and `edgesDrawn: 100_000` edges, the pair that together keeps the heap at 74 % of the cap (2,661 MB, 8.0 s), and `DataManager` refuses a load past either with `E_TOO_LARGE` (limit, count and held counts in `details`), so a consumer gets an error instead of a dead tab. Re-measure and raise once #394 and the per-style edge mesh land.

The defect this issue reports -- a load past what the renderer can hold kills the tab instead of failing, and the declared ceilings were numbers the renderer could never reach -- is fixed on master.

- Pull request #414 (commit b5abe279, "decline a load past the render ceiling instead of freezing") set `DEFAULT_LIMITS` in `graphty-element/src/session/limits.ts` to `renderCeiling: 50_000` nodes and `edgesDrawn: 100_000` edges, the pair measured in the comment above at 74 % of the V8 heap limit. `DataManager.refuseAboveCeiling` now rejects any load, `setNodes`/`setEdges` or streamed file past either with a `GraphtyError` coded `E_TOO_LARGE` before anything is added, so a consumer gets an error instead of a dead renderer.
- Pull request #394 (merged 2026-09-26) draws arrow heads as instances with one material per batch, which took the GPU process from 2.8 GB to 0.35 GB at 150,000 edges.

The remaining part of this issue's step 2 -- one mesh per style for edge lines and caps, so there is no per-edge scene object and the ceilings can be raised -- is tracked separately and stays open:

- #419 draw edges as instances so the renderer reaches a higher ceiling
- #444 2D lines, curves and patterned lines are still one mesh per edge
- #441 a test that fails if the renderer goes back to one scene object per edge

Closing this one as fixed; the ceiling increase continues in #419.

comments.body:
This is real and still present on master, but a proper fix needs a new public graphty-element API and a decision about how the field is edited, so it needs the owner.

What happens today. The style layer editor (`graphty/src/components/sidebar/panels/StyleLayerPropertiesPanel.tsx`) shows an `expression` selector as the raw JMESPath text in an editable field, and shows a `has` or `top` selector as a summary that also prints the raw path ("the elements carrying results.degree_0bkzd1n0p2dnik.value"). A channel bound to a run prints the same raw path ("from results.degree_...value"). So the run id leaks in three places, not one.

Why the app should not fix it on its own. graphty-element already knows the reader words for a path: `fieldWordsOf` in `graphty-element/src/session/GraphSession.ts` turns `results.<run>.value` into "Connections", and each run has a public `label`. But that lookup is private (only the legend uses it), and nothing in the element turns a whole selector into reader words. If the app rewrote paths inside expressions itself, it would be reimplementing element knowledge that every consumer needs, which the repository's rules forbid. The fix belongs in graphty-element, and that means adding public API.

Decisions needed:

1. The element API. Recommendation: one method on the styles surface, for example `session.styles.describeSelector(selector, target)`, returning the selector in reader words ("Connections (Degree, run 1) >= 9"), built on the existing `fieldWordsOf` plus the run label, plus a smaller `describePath(path, target)` for the bound-channel row and the `has`/`top` summaries. The names and return shape are published API.
2. How the field is edited. Showing reader words is easy; typing reader words back and parsing them into paths is a second grammar. Recommendation: show the reader-words description as the row, and keep the raw expression behind an explicit "Edit expression" action, so the stored JMESPath stays the only thing that is ever parsed. The alternative (a fully editable reader-words field) needs a reverse translation owned by the element.

Related work that should be considered together: the sets work in progress (feat/element-sets) is adding a `scope` selector kind and changing `session/styles/selector.ts`, and the design framework (`design/ui/framework/element-contract.md`, section on reading paths) plans `results.<result id>.<field>` paths keyed by result rather than run. A describe method written now should cover the `scope` kind and should word paths by result name where the result has one.

Rechecked on master on 2026-10-02: still present, and still waiting on the two decisions in the comment above (the name and shape of a public graphty-element method that describes a selector in reader words, and whether the Which nodes field stays raw text behind an Edit expression action). The app still prints the raw path in three places in graphty/src/components/sidebar/panels/StyleLayerPropertiesPanel.tsx: the expression text field, the has/top summaries, and the 'from <path>' line for a channel bound to a run. One change since that comment: the sets work has landed, so selectors now include a 'member' kind (a set's members), and the describe method should cover it too. Answering those two questions unblocks this; it stays labeled blocked until then.

Decision (owner, 2026-10-02): fix the name at its source instead of translating it. The describeSelector proposal above is dropped: it added a second, graphty-only vocabulary on top of JMESPath and hid what is stored.

Algorithms suggest a name for their result, the same way they suggest styles:

- An algorithm may declare an optional function, beside its style suggestions, that takes the run's settings and returns `{ id, label }`. The id is lowercase letters, digits and underscores (`pagerank`, `degree_in`, `louvain_resolution_1_5`) and becomes the result path (`results.degree_in.value >= 9`). The label is plain words ("PageRank (damping 0.85)") for rows, the legend and the style editor.
- An algorithm that suggests nothing gets its plain algorithm name as the id.
- graphty-element gives a new run the suggested id when it is free; reuses an existing run when one with the same settings already exists (the de-duplication the hash gives today); and adds `_2`, `_3`, ... when the id is taken by a run with different settings. A caller that names its run still wins.
- Renaming a run changes its label only, never the id selectors depend on.
- Saved files with today's hash ids keep loading unchanged; only new runs get readable ids.

With readable ids the "Which nodes" field, the has/top summaries and the bound-channel line all read correctly as plain JMESPath, with no translation layer.

comments.body:
I read the sabotage tests and the helper at current master and I do not think either failure mode described here can happen.

**A bare `toThrow()` cannot pass on the wrong exception.** In every sabotage test the lambda handed to `expect` contains exactly one call, `assertCheckPasses(report)`, and `report` is a plain `{ worst, worstLabel, samples }` object that was already computed on the line above. `assertCheckPasses` (`webgpu-graph-algorithms/test/helpers/sabotage.ts`, about line 2034) is a single `if (!(report.worst <= 1)) throw new Error("check failed: ...")`. It touches no GPU, no buffer and no other function, so the only exception it can throw is the "check failed" one. `toThrow()` and `toThrow(/check failed/)` are therefore equivalent there. In addition, each of these tests first asserts `expect(report.worst).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(mutation.minFactor)`, which is the stronger check: it requires the mutant to miss by a stated factor, not merely to fail.

**A mutant that crashes the kernel already shows up as its own outcome.** `withSabotage` runs outside any `expect(...).toThrow`, so if a mutant makes the kernel throw (a validation error, a device error), the exception propagates and the test fails, with that error in its output. Vitest reports a thrown error distinctly from an assertion failure. That is the result we want: a mutation row is meant to produce wrong numbers that the parity check catches, so a row that crashes the kernel instead is a broken row and should turn the test red rather than count as detection. Nothing in the current code lets a crash count as a pass.

Aligning the three bare `toThrow()` calls on `/check failed/` would only change their spelling, and adding a crash-versus-rejection outcome to `withSabotage` would build a way to expect crashes that no sabotage row should use. I am marking this blocked rather than closing it in case there is a concrete test run where a sabotage test passed or failed for the wrong reason. If there is one, please attach that output and I will reopen the question.

comments.body:
The mocks are real and they do drift, but the fix this issue proposes -- back the tests with a real headless session -- cannot be done as a test-only change today, so I am marking this blocked until the code under test can accept a session.

Why a session is not a drop-in for these mocks, at current master:

- Every mock helper returns the renderer class `Graph` (`test/helpers/mock-graph-context.ts`, `mock-graph-custom-data.ts`, `schema-test-graph.ts` all return `Graph`), because the code they feed takes a `Graph`. `Algorithm` is constructed as `new (g: Graph, options)` and reads `this.graph.getDataManager()` and `this.graph.acceleration` (`src/algorithms/Algorithm.ts`). `SchemaExtractor` takes a `Graph` and calls `getDataManager()`, `getNodeCount()` and `getEdgeCount()` (`src/ai/schema/SchemaExtractor.ts`). The AI command tests go through `CommandContext`, which also carries a `Graph`.
- A `GraphSession` from `createGraphSession()` is not a `Graph` and has no `DataManager`. Its own documentation (`graphty-element/session.ts`) says a session with no element behind it has no algorithm executor, because "every algorithm this package ships is built from the renderer", so `runs.start` answers `E_UNSUPPORTED`. The 28 algorithm test files among the 43 callers therefore cannot run on a standalone session at all.

So migrating these tests means first changing production code: the algorithms, `SchemaExtractor` and the AI commands would have to read from a session (or from a narrow interface a session satisfies) instead of from `Graph`. That is a real refactor of graphty-element internals, not test infrastructure, and it collides with the undo/redo work in flight (`feat/element-undo`, #427), which is rewriting every graphty-element mutation path through a command dispatcher and already edits `test/helpers/mockGraph.ts`.

Suggested order:

1. #26 first: where a test needs `Graph` behaviour, build a real `Graph` on a Babylon `NullEngine` instead of a hand-written mock. That removes the drift for the tests that most need it without any production change.
2. After #427 lands, move `Algorithm` and `SchemaExtractor` onto the session's data surface; this issue's migration then becomes mechanical, and a session-backed test helper is worth writing.

To unblock: either the owner confirms the production refactor in step 2 is wanted now (and after #427), or this issue is narrowed to the tests whose subject already reads from a session.

comments.body:
Re-checked against current master and the two most recent green runs of the GPU workflow on master (36265996913 and 36267932123, both 2026-09-26).

The lane is no longer approaching an hour. Both runs took 34 to 35 minutes from job start to finish, against the 75 minute timeout. Time per step in run 36267932123:

| Step | Time |
| --- | --- |
| Setup, checkout, pnpm install, build, adapter report, graph-format canary | about 2 min |
| node and node-limits projects | 16 min 16 s |
| node-device-errors | 26 s |
| node project again with subgroups disabled (the "twin" pass) | 10 min 5 s |
| node-device-errors again with subgroups disabled | 25 s |
| Browser smoke on NVIDIA | 1 min 10 s |
| graphty-element accelerated layout on NVIDIA | 48 s |
| Benchmarks and regression comparison | 3 min 26 s |

The two biggest contributors are the node plus node-limits step (the million-node limits file is about nine minutes of it, per the note in `gpu.yml`) and the no-subgroups twin pass. Inside each step vitest already runs test files in parallel (`webgpu-graph-algorithms/vitest.config.ts` gives the node pool `availableParallelism() - 1` forks, three on the 4 vCPU T4 machine), so there is no free parallelism left in the job itself.

The split the issue proposes has already been tried and does not work on the current provider. The header of `.github/workflows/gpu.yml` records it: machine.dev refused three matrix legs at once with "concurrent runner limit reached", and sequential legs never got a second machine. Splitting again needs a plan that allows more than one concurrent T4 runner, which is a paid-service decision.

That leaves three options, each of which is yours to decide:

1. Pay for concurrent runners on machine.dev and split tests and benchmarks (or the twin pass) onto separate jobs. Cuts wall-clock to roughly the longest leg (about 18 minutes) at the same per-minute cost plus the setup minutes of each extra leg.
2. Reduce coverage on the T4: for example run the no-subgroups twin pass only when the label `gpu` is on a pull request or on release commits, or move the million-node limits file out of every master push. Saves 9 to 10 minutes each, but removes NVIDIA coverage that runs nowhere else.
3. Keep the single job as it is, and only document a per-step time budget in `gpu.yml` and bring the timeout down to about 50 minutes so growth is noticed before it becomes a problem.

Recommendation: option 3 now. At 35 minutes the lane is well inside its timeout and the plan's runtime cap was lifted by the subscription, so the release wait is the only cost, and it does not justify paying for concurrency or dropping NVIDIA-only coverage. Revisit option 1 if the lane passes 45 minutes. If you agree, reply here and the budget and timeout change is a small edit to `gpu.yml`.

comments.body:
I disagree with the fix as written: a blanket deny on `git add`, `commit`, `push`, `checkout`, `switch`, `reset` and `restore` would break the way this repository is now worked on.

The premise is out of date. The only place on master that tells agents never to add, commit or push is one line in `webgpu-graph-algorithms/CLAUDE.md` ("Never `git add` / `commit` / `push` (the owner commits from `tmp/commit-p<N>.sh`)"), which dates from the phase when the owner committed that package by hand. It is not a repository-wide rule. Since then almost all changes, for example #457 through #462, have been made by coding agents that work on their own branch in a worktree under `.worktrees/`, commit with a signed commit through the commit-msg hook, push the branch and open a pull request. Master is protected by a ruleset, so no agent can push to it directly anyway. A checked-in deny list for those commands would block that whole workflow for every agent.

The commands that have actually caused damage are narrower:
- `git stash` in any checkout. In a subagent it can hang on an unanswered prompt, and in a shared worktree it takes other agents' uncommitted work with it.
- `git checkout` / `git switch` / `git reset` run in the main checkout (the repository root rather than a `.worktrees/` directory), which moves the branch out from under whoever is working there.

If a hook is wanted, I would recommend a `PreToolUse` hook that denies `git stash` everywhere and denies checkout, switch, reset and restore only when the working directory resolves to the main checkout (handling the `git -C <dir>` spelling), and leaves add, commit and push alone. The stale line in `webgpu-graph-algorithms/CLAUDE.md` should also be updated to match the worktree-and-PR workflow.

A checked-in agent permission policy is the owner's call, so I am labelling this blocked until the owner says which of these two directions to take: the narrow hook above, or the full deny list with the worktree workflow changed to go through a script the owner runs.

title: graphty-element: no test runs a registered layout or algorithm through an accelerator

comments.body:
Master now runs graphty-element's WebGPU path on a real device in CI and fails when it gets none. This landed with PR #21 (merged 2026-09-24).

- Launch flags: `graphty-element/vitest.config.ts` has a `BROWSER_GPU_FLAGS` table chosen by `GRAPHTY_BROWSER_GPU`. The `swiftshader` set is the same as the one in webgpu-graph-algorithms (`--enable-unsafe-webgpu --use-angle=swiftshader --enable-unsafe-swiftshader --use-webgpu-adapter=swiftshader`), and there are also sets for `nvidia`, `metal` and `warp`.
- The test: `graphty-element/test/browser/webgpu-layout.test.ts` imports the real `./webgpu` entry. Its first case asserts that the capabilities status reports `backend: "webgpu"`, and on NVIDIA it also checks the vendor. The later cases run forceatlas2, spring and spring-electrical, a drag, and PageRank, BFS and Dijkstra on the device, and compare the results with the CPU.
- Fails, not skips: the suite skips only when `GRAPHTY_BROWSER_GPU` is unset. When the flag is set and no adapter comes back, `beforeAll` fails waiting for "an accelerator to attach", and the attach assertion fails too.
- CI: `.github/workflows/gpu.yml` runs `vitest run --project=browser test/browser/webgpu-layout.test.ts` with `GRAPHTY_BROWSER_GPU=nvidia` on a T4. It does this on every master push and on pull requests labelled `gpu`, and `release.yml` will not publish unless that run is green. That is a real GPU rather than SwiftShader, which is a stronger check than the one this issue asked for.
- The story: the WebGPU stories in `stories/LayoutGpu.stories.ts` run in the Storybook shards, which have no WebGPU. So they attach the deterministic fake accelerator, and `assertRanOnTheFake` throws if the fake was not attached or never ran a batch. The stories therefore cannot pass quietly on the CPU path. The real-device check lives in the test above.

One gap is still open. The five ordinary CI browser shards on pull requests still launch without GPU flags, so an unlabelled pull request does not exercise the real device until it reaches master. Adding a SwiftShader shard to `ci.yml` is listed as an open question in `graphty-element/docs/decisions/G6.md`. It would take about 2 to 3 minutes of settle time per run on SwiftShader. If that is wanted, it belongs in its own issue. Closing this one.

comments.body:
Re-checked on 2026-09-26: the problem is still present. The repository is public, and `security_and_analysis` still reports secret scanning, push protection, validity checks and Dependabot security updates as disabled. CodeQL default setup reports `not-configured`, and no workflow on master uses CodeQL or `actions/dependency-review-action`.

Three of the four acceptance items are repository settings, not code, so they need the owner (someone with admin rights on graphty-org/graphty-monorepo) to switch them on. All of them are free for public repositories.

Recommendation, in Settings > Code security:
1. Enable secret scanning and push protection (and validity checks). Enabling it scans the existing history; rotate anything it reports (the Chromatic, Sentry and OpenAI tokens are the likely candidates if any were ever committed).
2. Enable CodeQL default setup for JavaScript/TypeScript and GitHub Actions. Default setup needs no workflow file and runs on pull requests and on master.
3. Enable Dependabot security updates (the dependency graph is already on for public repositories).

Or from the command line, as an admin:

    gh api -X PATCH repos/graphty-org/graphty-monorepo --input - <<'JSON'
    {"security_and_analysis":{"secret_scanning":{"status":"enabled"},
     "secret_scanning_push_protection":{"status":"enabled"},
     "dependabot_security_updates":{"status":"enabled"}}}
    JSON
    gh api -X PATCH repos/graphty-org/graphty-monorepo/code-scanning/default-setup -f state=configured

The fourth item, a `dependency-review` job on `pull_request` that fails on high or critical severity, is a small workflow change that can land as an ordinary pull request. It is held here only so that it lands together with the settings above; say the word and it will be added. If the dependency-review job should become a required check in the master ruleset, that is also a settings change only an admin can make.

comments.body: Decision (a reversible choice, made without waiting on the owner): Bundle the hand-model GLB files in the package and load them locally by default; no new config option.

Decision (2026-09-25): keep loading the XR hand models from the Babylon CDN for now.

Bundling the rigged hand GLBs and loading them locally needs `@babylonjs/loaders`, because core Babylon registers only the `.babylon` scene loader. Adding it as a runtime dependency makes every graphty-element consumer install and bundle it, and it has to move in lockstep with their `@babylonjs/core` version, for a feature only XR hand-tracking users need. So this issue stays open. The better route when it matters is to treat `@babylonjs/loaders` as an OPTIONAL peer, the way `@graphty/webgpu-graph-algorithms` is handled: present, the element loads the bundled hand models; absent, it keeps the CDN and says so.

The companion fix from the same branch -- XR gesture tests now drive the real XRInputHandler instead of copies of its maths (#206) -- ships independently.

Fixed on master by PR #399 (commit e7c44439, merged 2026-09-26).

- `graphty-element/src/xr/XRSessionManager.ts` now passes `OFFLINE_XR_OPTIONS` to both `enterVR` and `enterAR`. It sets `handSupportOptions.handMeshes.disableDefaultMeshes: true`, so Babylon never requests the rigged hand meshes or their shader from assets.babylonjs.com. Hands draw as Babylon's tracked joint spheres. The rigged meshes are glTF files and the element ships no glTF loader, so they never rendered even online: headsets see the same hands they did before.
- The same options stop the controller profile list download (`disableOnlineControllerRepository`) and load the near-interaction orb material from a JSON file shipped in the package (`src/xr/assets/touch-orb-material.json`) instead of snippet.babylonjs.com.
- `graphty-element/test/browser/xr-session.test.ts` has a test, "tracks and draws both hands without touching the network", that enters VR with hand tracking ON and emulated hands, checks both wrists are tracked and visible, and fails on any request to another host (every test in the file does).

No models were bundled and no config option was added, so there is no licence to record and no API change.

The earlier comment here saying hand models keep loading from the CDN is superseded by that change. Loading the rigged hand meshes locally would need `@babylonjs/loaders` as an optional peer; that is a feature, not this bug.

One request remains: a connected controller still downloads its model from controllers.babylonjs.com. That is tracked in #465.

This is owned by #427, undo and redo inside graphty-element, which is in progress on the `feat/element-undo` branch.

The problem described here -- a history store in the app that records steps but cannot reverse any of them -- cannot be fixed correctly in the app. Reversing a style-layer edit, a deleted result or a layout switch means snapshotting or inverting graph-element state, and the architecture rules put that inside graphty-element so every consumer gets it. #427 does exactly that: every graphty-element mutation goes through one dispatcher that records a forward and inverse change, and the session exposes `undo()`, `redo()`, `canUndo` / `canRedo` and a labelled history. comments.body:
The open question in this issue (are notes app data or graph data?) is answered by the committed design: notes belong to graphty-element. `design/element-api/element-api-design.md` gives every session a `readonly notes: NotesApi` member (line 619, section 4.15.3), and the UI framework's element contract lists Note as element-owned data saved in the session part of the project file. That element work is tracked in #145, which is not started.

So this issue splits in two:

- Now, in the graphty app: stop discarding text. The node inspector's Notes input gets disabled with a Coming tag, the same treatment the edge inspector's Notes section already has, and the Add note shortcut stops pretending to work. This is the "until the store exists" acceptance item.
- Later, after #145 lands: the app reads and writes `session.notes` for the inspectors, Mark done, Delete and the case-note count. The app must not grow its own note store in the meantime, because that would be exactly the app-side workaround the architecture forbids.

Removing the needs-decision label, since the decision is recorded in the design.

The interim part of this issue is done in #482: the node inspector now draws its note box disabled with a Coming tag, the same way the edge inspector draws its Notes, and the save path that cleared typed text and opened Explore is gone. Nothing a reader types can be lost any more.

The rest -- storing notes, showing them after a reload, Mark done, Delete, and the real case-note count -- waits on graphty-element's session notes (#145). The app must not keep its own note store in the meantime. This issue stays open until #145 lands and the inspectors are wired to it.

graphty-element now carries notes as `session.notes` (merged in #674), so this is no longer blocked. The fix is on branch `fix/app-notes-from-element-session`; a pull request follows.

What the branch does, all as a consumer of the element (the app keeps no note store of its own):

- The node inspector's note box works again. Cmd/Ctrl+Enter adds a note about the selected node through `session.notes.add`; Escape clears the box. The notes about that node are listed under it.
- Delete calls `session.notes.remove`, which is one step in the element's history, so Undo brings the note back.
- The app reads the notes again whenever the element reports `note:changed`, so a write, an undo, a redo or an opened project all show up.
- The graph summary's case-note count is the number of notes about the whole graph. Clicking it opens the Explore panel with its Notes section expanded.
- The N key focuses the note box of the selected node, or opens the case notes when nothing is selected.
- The edge inspector uses the same Notes section, ready for when the app can select an edge.

What is left, and why:

- Mark done: the element's notes have no done state, so the Done checkbox is removed rather than kept in the app. Whether notes get one is a change to the saved notes format and needs the owner's decision: #705.
- Surviving a page reload: the element holds notes in the session, and saving and reopening a whole session waits on #301.
- Notes on a multi-node selection stay marked Coming: an element note names at most 64 targets, so a note about a larger selection needs the selection kept as a set first.
- The Explore panel's Notes section still lists nothing and has no box for a note about the whole graph, so a case note cannot yet be written from the app. That is a separate change to the Explore panel.
The remaining Explore panel work -- listing the case notes and writing a note about the whole graph -- is tracked in #707.

Pull request https://github.com/graphty-org/graphty-monorepo/pull/717 wires the node inspector's notes to graphty-element's session notes, so a typed note is saved, listed, deletable and undoable, and the graph summary shows the real case-note count. Merging it closes this issue; a Done state is tracked in #705, notes surviving a reload in #301, and Explore's empty Notes section in #707.

comments.body:
This is still real on master: the palette placeholder still promises "Search commands, nodes and edges" (graphty/src/components/shell/CommandPalette.tsx:36) and `matches()` still compares only a command row's group and label.

The fix cannot be done in the app alone, and the piece graphty-element is missing is a new public API, so it needs your decision before anyone builds it.

What the element has today (commit 766173a8, which closed #3): a text search, but only as a selection change. `element.session.selection.apply({ text: "..." })` replaces the selection with every node the text matches. The search itself (`find` in graphty-element/src/session/query.ts) is internal: it returns node hits only (no edges), in index order, with no cap and no exact-match-first ranking. There is no read-only way for any consumer to ask "which elements would this text match?" and show them as a list before choosing one, which is what a palette (or any search box with suggestions) needs. There is also no public "bring this node into view" call; the element exposes `zoomToFit()` for the whole graph only.

Building the palette rows in the app by walking the graph's nodes would be the app reimplementing element search, which CLAUDE.md forbids.

Decision needed: add a public, read-only search to graphty-element. My recommendation:

- `element.session.search(text, { limit?: number, kinds?: ("node" | "edge")[] })` returning `{ hits: { id, kind, label? }[], total: number, truncated: boolean }`, using the same text modes as `selection.apply({ text })` (plain, `exact:`, `regex:`, `id:`, `attr:`), ranked exact id or label match first, capped at `limit` (default 50).
- A way to frame one element, for example `element.zoomToElements(ids)` or a selection option that frames what it selected.

With those, the app change is small: a "Nodes" / "Edges" group in the palette fed by `session.search`, and choosing a row calls `selection.apply({ ids: [...] })` and frames it. Until the API exists, the cheapest honest fix is to change the placeholder to "Search commands" so the palette stops promising what it cannot do; say if you want that done now.

Related open feature: #175 (commands missing from the palette) edits the same `paletteItems` list in AppShell.tsx and should land in the same change or be sequenced with it.

Rechecked on current master (2026-10-02). Half of what this issue was waiting on has landed: graphty-element now has a public `element.zoomToNodes(ids, options)` (commit eec1e9b5d, with a follow-up in b3d539b93 that frames a lone node), so choosing a node row can select it with `selection.apply({ ids })` and bring it into view with no new element API.

The other half is still missing. The palette needs a read-only text search that lists matching nodes and edges before anything is chosen, ranked with an exact id or label match first and capped for large graphs. graphty-element still has only `selection.apply({ text })`, which replaces the selection, and its internal `find` (graphty-element/src/session/query.ts, wired in GraphSession.ts:2270) returns node hits only, uncapped and in index order. Building the list in the app by walking nodes would be the app reimplementing element search, which the project rules forbid.

So the decision still needed is only the search API: whether to add a public `element.session.search(text, { limit, kinds })` returning `{ hits: { id, kind, label }[], total, truncated }` (or another shape you prefer). It is a new public API, so it waits for you. Keeping the blocked label until then.

Still present on master: `SortableLayerItem` in `graphty/src/components/layout/LeftSidebar.tsx` is a hand-styled `Box` holding only the name and the drag handle. The row has no show/hide, no delete, no paint chip and no match count.

Two parts can be built with the element as it is: show/hide through `session.styles.update(id, { enabled })` and delete through `session.styles.remove(id)`. The element already refuses to delete its own base and selection layers with `E_PROTECTED`, and `Layer.locked` gives the reason for the disabled button.

One part needs a decision first, because it adds to graphty-element's published API:

**The match count.** graphty-element does not report how many elements a layer matched. `StylesApi` has `list`, `get`, `validate`, `legend` and `explain`, and none of them returns a count. The issue correctly says the app must not count them itself. So the element needs a new public read, and choosing its name and shape is a one-way door. The design framework also defines the count differently from the artboard this issue cites. `design/ui/framework/conceptual-model.md` (around line 745) and `glossary.md` (the Hide/Show entry) say a layer that takes elements to opacity 0 counts what it hid ("412 at opacity 0"). The artboard says "N nodes matched". Those are different numbers.

Recommendation: add one synchronous read to `StylesApi`, for example `styles.matched(id): { nodes: number; edges: number }`. It would be computed from the same selector pass the repaint already makes, so it adds no cost. It would carry edges as well as nodes, because edge layers exist. The "at opacity 0" figure would be left for later, as a derived label. Please confirm the name and shape, or choose another.

Other work this row depends on:
- The row component: PR #409 rebuilds compact-mantine's row family (`ActionRow`, `ToggleRow`, `TrailingSlot` and others). Building this row on today's compact-mantine means rebuilding it once #409 merges, so the row work should wait for #409.
- Undoing a delete belongs to the element undo work (#427, and #197 for the app side).
- Grouping a run's layers under one parent is #171, which touches the same list.

Once the count API is decided and #409 has merged, this can be fixed as a single change: the element read, then the row built on the compact-mantine row with the chip, name, count, eye and delete.

Re-checked on current master (2026-10-02). Nothing has changed, so this stays blocked for the two reasons in the earlier comment.

1. graphty-element still has no public read for how many nodes and edges a layer matched. StylesApi offers list, get, validate, legend and explain, and none of them returns a count. Adding one is a new published API, so it needs the owner to confirm the name and shape. The proposal is styles.matched(id) returning { nodes, edges }.
2. PR #409, which rebuilds the compact-mantine row components this row should be built from, is still open. Building the row now would mean building it twice.

What unblocks it: a reply confirming or replacing the count API, and #409 merged. After that it is one change: the element read first, then the row built on the shared compact-mantine row with the paint chip, name, count, show/hide and delete. Grouping a run's layers (#171) touches the same list and should come after, not in the same change.

comments.body:
Root cause found, and it is not the driver. A `Kernel` in webgpu-graph-algorithms caches its bind groups for the life of the context, and that cache had no limit. The layout models cleared only some kernels on dispose, so each disposed grid simulation left 84 bind groups behind, with their native descriptor sets. A heap snapshot of 200 simulations shows it directly.

A raw Dawn loop with no graphty code stays flat on lavapipe and on the RTX 4070 SUPER. Through graphty, the NVIDIA card grows the same way lavapipe does. No Dawn or Mesa report is needed.

PR #495 bounds the cache to the 32 most recently bound buffer sets per kernel. On lavapipe, the 4,096-seed unbiasedness test now peaks at 497 MB per worker instead of 3.99 GB, and both cases pass the tolerance at 4,096 seeds. The measurements and the repro script are in `webgpu-graph-algorithms/docs/grid-memory-retention.md` and `webgpu-graph-algorithms/scripts/grid-memory.mjs`.

Still open on this issue: restoring the 4,096-seed assertion on the software lane and deleting `UNBIASED_SEEDS_SOFTWARE`. That lands as a follow-up once the change to the grid parity helpers merges. Dawn 0.6.1 could not be measured here (it needs a newer libstdc++ than Ubuntu 22.04 has). The cause was in this package, so the Dawn version does not change the result.

Checked against current master: the bug is real. `ScreenshotCapture` still hands the whole capture to Babylon's `CreateScreenshotAsync` (graphty-element/src/screenshot/ScreenshotCapture.ts, around line 444), `ScreenshotOptions` in graphty-element/src/screenshot/types.ts has no legend setting, and nothing under src/screenshot reads the legend model. The model it would draw from is already public as `styles.legend()`, which returns `LegendBlock[]` built headlessly by `buildLegend` in session/styles/legend.ts. The design framework also asks for this: export settings include "legend and its placement" (design/ui/framework/conceptual-model.md, Export), and an exported legend must carry its scope in its title (design/ui/framework/principles.md).

The fix itself is contained. After the scene capture, draw the `LegendBlock[]` onto a 2D canvas at the export's pixel size, composite it over the scene image, then encode. What blocks it is a naming decision: the fix adds a new field to `ScreenshotOptions`, which is an exported type of a published package. Once released, renaming or reshaping that field is a breaking change.

Decision needed: approve the shape of the new option, or give a different one.

Recommendation, additive and optional, with nothing changing for existing callers:

```ts
legend?: boolean | {
    position?: "top-left" | "top-right" | "bottom-left" | "bottom-right"; // default "bottom-right"
    title?: string; // default: the scope the legend describes, per the framework principle
};
```

`legend: true` means the defaults. Leaving the option out, or passing `false`, keeps today's output. The drawn legend scales with `multiplier` and `enhanceQuality`, so text stays sharp at print sizes. This is the "legend: true with a position" the issue suggests, with the position values spelled out. Once the shape is approved, the acceptance criteria in the issue (a browser test that compares the legend region with and without the option, plus a documented example) can go ahead unchanged.

Rechecked on master as of 2026-10-02: still unfixed, and no open pull request touches the screenshot code or the legend. This stays blocked on the same decision as the earlier comment: the shape of the new legend option on `ScreenshotOptions`, an exported type of the published graphty-element package.

One thing to weigh when deciding: feature #292 (an opt-in on-canvas legend drawn by the element itself) asks for the same legend renderer and for its own position and size options, and lists "screenshot option to include it" as one of its acceptance items. If the screenshot option and the on-canvas legend option share one spelling (for example the same position values and the same defaults), both can be built from one renderer in one change. Approving one option shape that covers both issues would unblock both.

To unblock: approve the proposed `legend?: boolean | { position?, title? }` shape, or give a different one, and say whether #292's on-canvas legend should use the same shape.

Confirmed on current master: this is a real defect. `line.width` has three live meanings in graphty-element/src/meshes/EdgeMesh.ts:
- 3D solid and bezier edges (lines 536 and 273): `width * 20` screen pixels in CustomLineRenderer. These shrink with depth (CustomLineRenderer.ts:143-147) and do not grow when you zoom in.
- Patterned edges in 2D and 3D, and 2D solid edges (lines 300 and 315): `width / 40` world units. These scale with zoom.
- Animated edges (line 585): the raw `width` as a GreasedLine width, a third scale. The GreasedLine fallback at line 560 is dead code (USE_CUSTOM_RENDERER = true).

The design docs picked these on purpose and they disagree. edge-styles-implementation-plan.md:3898 chose screen pixels for 3D solid edges. 2d-edge-design.md:477 chose world units for 2D. Patterned edges are world-space meshes. Any fix changes the rendered size of at least one whole class of edges in every existing graph, so the unit is a public styling contract and needs an owner decision before work starts.

Decision needed (reply with "Decision: A" or "Decision: B", plus the answer to question 2):

A) World units everywhere. Edges grow and shrink with zoom, like nodes do. CustomLineRenderer (3D solid and bezier) and the animated edges move to world units. Patterned and 2D edges keep their current look. 3D solid edges change: they get thicker up close and thinner far away.

B) Screen pixels everywhere. An edge is the same number of pixels at any zoom. The patterned, 2D solid and animated renderers move to screen-space sizing. That means rewriting the patterned-mesh sizing, which is more work. 3D solid edges keep their current look. Patterned and 2D edges change.

Question 2 (only matters for B): should width still taper with depth in 3D, as it does today, or stay a constant pixel width?

Once decided, the fix is one width conversion used by every line renderer (replacing the * 20 and / 40 constants), a browser test that measures a solid and a patterned edge at two zoom levels, and the unit stated in the EdgeStyle schema doc and docs/guide/styling.md.

Labelled `blocked` and `needs-decision`: the unit for `line.width` is part of the published style contract, so the owner picks it.

comments.body:
Triage: disagree as filed (not a critical defect).

The shader line is real. graphty-element/src/meshes/FilledArrowRenderer.ts:127 computes `right = normalize(cross(forward, toCamera))` and nothing guards the case where the two vectors are exactly parallel. But the visible behaviour the ticket expects cannot come from fixing it.

1. Every 3D arrowhead is flat, and its plane contains the edge direction. createTriangle, createDiamond, createBox, createCircle and the other shapes all place their vertices at y=0. The vertex shader maps them to `x*forward + z*right`, so the arrowhead always lies in a plane that contains `forward`. When the camera is on the edge's line, the view ray runs along `forward`, so that plane is seen exactly edge-on whatever fallback axis `right` gets. The arrowhead projects to a zero-area segment and no pixels are rasterised. A fallback axis cannot make it "face-on", and the acceptance check (arrowhead pixels present with the camera on the edge axis) cannot pass with this geometry.

2. The NaN only happens at exact alignment. With highp floats, a nearly parallel cross product is small but non-zero and normalizes fine. At the exact alignment the correct image is an invisible edge-on arrowhead anyway, and the NaN only drops that one triangle.

3. The "spin" near alignment is the billboard working as designed. `right` rotates around the line to keep the face toward the camera, and near the axis the arrowhead is a thin sliver whose orientation follows the camera.

If the goal is for arrowheads to stay visible when you look straight down an edge, that is a geometry feature: a cone, or a cap perpendicular to the line for end-on views. Please refile it as a feature request if that is wanted. Adding an epsilon guard to the cross product is fine as a one-line hardening, but it changes no rendered pixel.

Related: #122 edits the same file.

Labelled `blocked`: reopen with a revised expectation if the owner disagrees.

comments.body:
Triage of the high-priority bugs: I disagree with this ticket as filed, so I have labelled it blocked for the owner's review.

I looked into this and do not think it is a reachable bug, so I am marking it blocked rather than fixing it.

The code facts are right: wcc-compress breaks on maxSteps without setting the changed flag, and checkLabels only checks that labels are in range. But a split component cannot come out of the round loop in components.ts (lines 292-323), for these reasons:

- Only two things ever write comp[]. The first is a successful CAS hook in link_pair, which always sets the flag, and a link walk that hits the step cap also sets it. The second is a compress store, which only ever replaces a node's pointer with one of its ancestors.
- The flag is cleared once per batch, and each batch runs 4 link+compress pairs. The loop exits only when a whole batch ends with the flag at 0. So in the last batch there were no hooks and the forest's structure did not change. That batch then runs 4 compress passes on a fixed forest, and the final compress at line 327 makes 5.
- Every load in a compress walk returns an ancestor at least one original hop further up, so a walk capped at 1024 steps still moves v at least 1024 hops up. Depth drops to at most about ceil(d/1024) per pass: from any n < 2^32, to 2^22, then 2^12, then 4, then 1. Every label is a root before the final compress even runs.
- A capped compress in an earlier batch just leaves a shorter path. The next link round climbs it and then hooks or hits its cap, either of which sets the flag, so another batch runs. This is what the kernel's doc comment describes.

Empirical check on master, NVIDIA RTX 4070 SUPER (Dawn): connectedComponents with renumber:false on path graphs of 5k, 50k, 500k and 2M nodes, each in ordered, reversed and randomly shuffled node order. The ordered case builds an n-deep hook chain in the sampled round. Every run returned count 1, and labels[labels[v]] == labels[v] held for every node.

A host-side check that labels[labels[v]] == labels[v], throwing E_VALIDATION when it fails, would only guard against a device that does not do what it says. That is the same reasoning as the existing range check. It would be reasonable as optional hardening, but it would not fix a bug. If you have a graph or a device where the count comes out wrong, please attach it and I will reopen this as a bug.
Closing on the owner's decision: not a reachable bug (see the analysis above). Reopen with a graph or device where the component count comes out wrong.

- tools/check-published-deps.mjs allows graph-format, and only graph-format, to be declared both ways (the "same name in both" rule and DEPENDENCY_AND_PEER_ALLOWED).
- The "hand-written ^1.0.0 goes stale" risk is already guarded. The same script checks every internal @graphty/* range, peers included, against the version in the workspace (semver.satisfies over peerDependencies). If graph-format moves to 2.0.0 while a peer still says ^1.0.0, the published-deps check fails before release. It cannot drift silently the way the webgpu peer once did.
- The ERESOLVE case needs a graph-format 2.x, and none exists (the current version is 1.0.4). When 2.0 lands, widening each peer is a deliberate step that the check above forces.
- Making the peer workspace:^ would publish it as ^<current version> and narrow what an application can share, which is the opposite of what the peer is there for.

This is still open on master: there is no sonar-project.properties, no Sonar step in any workflow under .github/workflows/, nothing in tools/prepush.sh, and no Sonar secret in the repository's Actions secrets.

The work cannot start until the owner makes these calls, because each one is a paid service, an organisation setting or a credential:

1. Which instance. Recommendation: SonarQube Cloud (sonarcloud.io). It is free for public repositories, needs no server to run, and imports the Vitest LCOV reports the CI coverage job already produces. A self-hosted server only makes sense if the repository is, or will become, private and a paid Cloud plan is unwanted.
2. Create the organisation and project in that instance, bound to graphty-org/graphty-monorepo. Recommendation: one project for the whole monorepo, with sonar.sources and sonar.tests listing each package directory, so one quality gate covers every package and one required check is added.
3. Add the token as the Actions secret SONAR_TOKEN (and tell us the organisation key and project key).
4. Decide whether the quality gate becomes a required status check in the master ruleset. Recommendation: yes, but only after it has run green on a few pull requests.

On pre-push: the Sonar scanner needs the server to compute the quality gate, so a local run needs network access and a token on every developer machine and adds a full upload and server-side analysis to each push. Recommendation: keep the gate in CI only, and do not add it to tools/prepush.sh; the pre-push gate already runs lint and knip, which catch most of what a local scan would. If you want it locally anyway, say so and it will be added behind SONAR_TOKEN being set, skipped with a printed notice when it is not.

Once the secret and keys exist, the CI side is a small change: a sonar-project.properties at the root and one job after the coverage merge that runs the scanner against the merged LCOV report.
Pull request: https://github.com/graphty-org/graphty-monorepo/pull/725

The same crash now shows up on Linux (lavapipe), not only on macOS.

On 2026-09-26 the CI job "Test (webgpu-graph-algorithms-node)" failed on three pull requests that were started within one minute of each other: #367 (run 36248573702), #369 (run 36248578705) and #399 (run 36248619085). #369 changes only graph-io and #399 changes only graphty-element, so the pull requests did not cause it.

All three fail the same way:

- vitest reports `Error: Channel closed` / `ERR_IPC_CHANNEL_CLOSED` from tinypool: the forked worker process died.
- The shard wrapper reports `[missing-files] started 85, reported 84, missing 1` and `no result for test/node/entry.test.ts`. It is the same file each time.

`test/node/entry.test.ts` is the one test file that goes around the test-setup workaround described above. It creates its own Dawn instances through `createNodeGpu()`, `createNodeGpuContext()` and `probeNodeWebGpu()`, then drops them through `dispose()` (`probeNodeWebGpu` drops its handle in a `finally`). That is the drop-then-garbage-collect sequence this issue describes, where Dawn's AsyncRunner goes on polling an instance that has been freed. So the worker running that file is the one that dies. The same file passes on the other runs from the same period (for example 36249632916, 36248691023 and 36254278343), which fits an intermittent use-after-free.

What this adds to the issue: the crash is not specific to Metal, so the acceptance test should also run on the Linux lavapipe lane. Until the entry point is fixed, `entry.test.ts` can take down the `node` project in normal CI.

Still present on master: `compactMultiValueStyles` in compact-mantine/src/theme/styles/inputs.ts sets a fixed `minHeight: 24`, and graphty/src/theme.ts still has argument-less `vars: () => ({...})` resolvers for NativeSelect and ColorInput.

All of this issue, including the DataTable search field size, is fixed by the open pull request #364. It makes the multi-value field height follow `--input-height`, moves the NativeSelect and ColorInput size handling into compact-mantine, corrects the story labels and adds browser tests that measure the rendered heights. That PR is waiting on review, alongside the compact-mantine rebuild in #409, which touches the same files. Leaving this issue open until one of them merges.
